title: Declare acceptance boundary kinds only from the controlled vocabulary

facts.note: Acceptance spec files (planner-authored) are identifiable by path/file kind.
Task text mentions declaring, reviewing or validating the integration surfaces an acceptance exercises.

values: boundary_kind value added or edited in an acceptance
facts.note: Diff-level observer that extracts boundary_kind values from acceptance declarations.
Validator finding on any acceptance, including unchanged declarations already containing unknown values.
Whether the planner is authoring, revising or reviewing acceptance boundary declarations.

fires: A planner writes an acceptance that declares boundary_kind values.
A planner edits an existing acceptance's boundary declaration (adds, renames or removes a boundary_kind).
A planner reviews or validates existing acceptances and finds a boundary_kind value (unchanged or not) outside the vocabulary, e.g. `golden`.
A planner is deciding whether a golden-file comparison belongs in the acceptance's boundary_kind list.
doesNotFire: Acceptance edits that neither add, change nor review boundary_kind declarations.
Editing only harness_code values with no boundary_kind involved (governed by the harness-code vocabulary, not this rule).
Production code changes that introduce a new integration surface without any acceptance boundary declaration being written or reviewed.

given: An acceptance declares the named integration surfaces (boundary_kind values) it exercises
when: You write, edit or review its boundary_kind entries
then: Use only values from the controlled boundary_kind vocabulary: argv, subprocess, filesystem, git, http_wire, llm_wire, cmux_rpc, env_config, db_wire, event_wire.
prefer: Pick the value whose definition matches the surface exercised: argv = command-line argument vector passed to a process; subprocess = a child process spawned and observed; filesystem = files and directories read or written; git = a local git repository's objects, refs and config; http_wire = HTTP request/response envelopes (cassette when hermetic); llm_wire = LLM prompt/response envelopes (recorded/deterministic when hermetic); cmux_rpc = cmux RPC request/response messages; env_config = environment variables and configuration inputs; db_wire = database query/response envelopes; event_wire = event-bus publish/consume envelopes.
avoid: Inventing, abbreviating or synonym-ing boundary_kind values outside the vocabulary — unknown values are rejected by tester.acceptance-violation.hermetic-fake-must-declare-contract.
Listing `golden` as a boundary_kind: `golden` is a harness_code, NOT a boundary_kind (Decision #7).
why: boundary_kind is a controlled vocabulary of named integration surfaces an acceptance exercises; unknown values are rejected.
evidence: tester.acceptance-violation.hermetic-fake-must-declare-contract reports no unknown boundary_kind values for the acceptance.
Every boundary_kind in the acceptance is one of the ten vocabulary values and none is `golden`.
verifier_detail: Validator: tester.acceptance-violation.hermetic-fake-must-declare-contract rejects any boundary_kind value not in the vocabulary.
Term boundary_kind: a named integration surface exercised by an acceptance.
argv: Command-line argument vector passed to a process.
subprocess: A child process spawned and observed.
filesystem: Files and directories read or written.
git: A local git repository's objects, refs, and config.
http_wire: HTTP request/response envelopes (cassette when hermetic).
llm_wire: LLM prompt/response envelopes (recorded/deterministic when hermetic).
env_config: Environment variables and configuration inputs.
`golden` is a harness_code, NOT a boundary_kind (Decision #7); a boundary_kind of `golden` is an unknown value.
